title: The design document is the build spec
statement: Write a lesson from its own design document and audit the built lesson part by part against it, because builds drop or adapt designed parts silently.
example: One lesson was authored, reviewed and deployed missing three components its design document required.
detail: The reading project corrected its order of authority: the build spec for a lesson is its own design document, not the more general workbook or procedure page, and one lesson as authored, reviewed and deployed had been missing three components its design document mandated. Its spec-first build routine was reported proven over three lessons, with defects falling each time and the last shipping zero content-validator defects, though that is a self-report over consecutive lessons and is confounded with the team's own learning. A later brief found curriculum alignment verified at the passage level but not yet at the programme level. Write a lesson only once the course plan is fixed (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/curriculum-agent.md`), turn its design into a build spec before authoring, record why each item format was chosen (`grade3-reading/artifacts/team-direction-2026-09-09/GATE-STANDARD-DRAFT.md`), and audit the built lesson against the whole programme as well.
against: The same brief calls the programme-level gap an open scope question, not a defect (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0218-devfactory-review-and-decision-brief-2026-09-10.qmd`, lines 87-89). Not every gap is a defect: a programme-level mismatch with prescribed materials was ruled an open scope question, not a defect (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0218-devfactory-review-and-decision-brief-2026-09-10.qmd`, lines 86-89).

**"named designs govern"** made the four original Peter Pan lesson-design DOCX (`~/Downloads/5. Curriculum`, PP1-PP4) the build specification for L4-L7, not the sourcing portal's 17-chapter novel.

**Slot 3, Aladdin Part 3, is MISSING outright** — spec slot real, design doc exists on disk, but no lessonId was ever authored/shipped for it.

**defect count tracks build order and spec quality, not review count.** L5 (built from a packet + doc, first of the arc) drifted most; L7 (built last, from a spec that carried every rule earned during the week) shipped cleanest despite being the only never-human-reviewed lesson.
Defect density anti-correlates with spec completeness, not with human review count — evidence: L7 (never reviewed, best spec) vs L5 (reviewed era, thin spec).
